According to the document "Sustainable Direct Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Solvent Recovery of Electrode Materials" (cssc-2020), at 160 °C, delamination takes about 6 seconds. At the boiling point of ethylene glycol (198 °C), delamination takes about 2 seconds.

To find out how many times faster delamination is at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C, we can divide the time it takes at 160 °C (6 seconds) by the time it takes at the boiling point (2 seconds):

6 seconds / 2 seconds = 3

So, delamination at the boiling point of ethylene glycol is 3 times faster than at 160 °C.
